1502.body:
## What happens

Four rules in `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` draw secondary text at `#808080`, `#8c8c8c` and `#a6a6a6`. All of it is normal-size text — 11 px, 12 px, 12.5 px — so WCAG 2.1 AA applies at **4.5:1** (SC 1.4.3; the large-text exemption starts at 18 pt, or 14 pt bold). Measured against the surfaces they actually render on, every one is below the floor, and two of them are below 3:1:

| rule | colour | size | surface it is drawn on | contrast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.settings-field-hint` | `#808080` | 12.5 px | `#fff` — the settings panel (`.config-panel` and `.config-backdrop` are `#fff`; `.settings-main` is `#fff`) | **3.95:1** |
| the same rule inside `.settings-ability-option.is-selected` | `#808080` | 12.5 px | `#f4f8ff` (`--primary-softer`) | **3.71:1** |
| `.session-flyout-desc` | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` — `.session-menu-flyout` is `#fff` | **3.36:1** |
| the same rule while its row is hovered | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#f5f5f5` — `.session-flyout-row:hover` | **3.08:1** |
| `.session-flyout-note` (added for #1330, same colour) | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` | **3.36:1** |
| `.expert-note` | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` — the 专家 flyout | **3.36:1** |
| `.doc-tab-hint` | `#a6a6a6` | 11 px | `#f0f0f0` (`--surface-sunk`, the workspace panel) or `#fff` inside a `.workspace-section` | **2.14:1 / 2.43:1** |

Ratios are WCAG 2.1 relative luminance against the background named in the same row.

The two darkest cases are worth naming on their own: `#a6a6a6` on `#f0f0f0` is **2.14:1**, and `#8c8c8c` on the hover row is **3.08:1** — the second one only appears while the pointer is over the row the reader is reading, which is exactly when they need it.

## These are user-visible text, not decoration

- `.settings-field-hint` carries the sentence under a settings field: the skill-name rule (`TEXT.settings.skills.nameHint`, and `nameInvalid` in the same element), the specialist instructions hint and the capability hint (`TEXT.settings.system.specialists.instructionsHint`, `capabilitiesHint`) — `views/settings/SkillForm.tsx`, `views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx`. Only the `is-error` variant switches to `--danger`, and that one is not part of this report.
- `.expert-note` carries the flyout's own status: `TEXT.composer.expertsLoading` (“正在读取专家…”) and `TEXT.composer.expertsEmpty` (“没有匹配的专家。”) — `views/Composer.tsx`.
- `.session-flyout-desc` carries the line that explains what each choice does, under the label of every row of 审查档位, 请求批准 and 会话设置.
- `.doc-tab-hint` carries the folder that tells two same-named documents apart in the tab strip — `views/WorkspacePanel.tsx`.

None of them is an icon, a placeholder, a disabled control or decorative text, so none of them is exempt.

## Where it comes from

`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` at `main` `d9f5a3da`:

- `:2208` `.session-flyout-desc { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2216` `.session-flyout-note { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2442` `.expert-note { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2993` `.doc-tab-hint { color: #a6a6a6; font-size: 11px; … }`
- `:4225` `.settings-field-hint { color: #808080; font-size: 12.5px; … }`

Two of the three colours are already tokens, so the fix is at token level rather than per selector: `apps/desktop/src/styles/tokens.css:36` `--text-faint: #8c8c8c`, `:35` `--muted-light: #a6a6a6`; `#808080` is written literally. The surfaces in the table are `--surface: #ffffff` (`:20`), `--surface-sunk: #f0f0f0` (`:24`), `--surface-hover: #ededed` (`:23`), `--primary-softer: #f4f8ff` (`:41`), and `.session-flyout-row:hover { background: #f5f5f5 }` (`:2177`).

## Suggested fix

Move all three to one secondary-text value that clears 4.5:1 on the worst surface in the table:

| candidate | on `#fff` | on `#f5f5f5` | on `#f0f0f0` | on `#f4f8ff` | on `#ededed` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#666666` | 5.74 | 5.27 | 5.04 | 5.39 | 4.90 |
| `#777777` (today's `--muted`) | 4.48 | 4.11 | 3.93 | 4.20 | 3.83 |

`#666666` is the value already agreed for the desktop sidebar hints in #1486, which is the same defect on a different surface; using it here as well keeps one secondary colour across the desktop instead of a third shade. Note that `--muted` (`#777777`) does **not** clear the floor on the darker surfaces, so it cannot simply be reused.

## Related

#1486 reports the same problem for the sidebar and the landing surface. This report is the settings, flyout and document-tab half of it; the two do not overlap.

## Environment

- Windows 11, desktop renderer (React in Chromium), zh-CN and en.
- Colour values, surfaces and sizes read from `apps/desktop/src/styles` at `main` `d9f5a3da8c281829d6791efbbe3ce9392bf936b6`; ratios computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula.
- No backend, no data and no behaviour involved: this is a stylesheet and token change.
1502.title: [Bug]: Desktop settings, flyout and document-tab hint text misses WCAG AA (2.14:1 – 3.95:1)

1506.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing Issues and PRs for `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`; nothing tracks this failure (the only hit is merged PR #1361, which introduced the check).
- [x] I reproduced the reconciliation failure locally at `e63099ab` with synthetic mocked artifacts; no E2E stack was started.
- [x] This reports a CI reconciliation regression, not a product failure: all 195 planned mocked cases passed in this run.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

[Dispatch Nightly #113](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46030598150) (attempt 1, `main @ e63099ab3b0b2bb30e9ecea432ee6be69efcc8a1`, `profile=daily`, `backend=jiuwenswarm`, `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`) failed **only** in `Gate / merge-gate` (job `140705976460`), step `Reconcile mocked results`:

```
##[group]Run node .ci/mocked-report.mjs .ci-mocked-plan/plan.json .ci-mocked-results .ci-results
### Mocked E2E: FAIL

Planned 195; executed 195; passed 195.

- standard-config: UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS

##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The mocked layer that produced those artifacts was green: `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` (job `140613911090`) concluded **success** with `| e2e | 58a08ac09c38 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |` (75/75 passed, 1 passed after retry), and the other four mocked shards were green too. `Report the outcome` (job `140706111813`) then failed with `RESULT: failure` for the same reason. So the failure is purely in result reconciliation.

#### Root cause

1. `test/support/tagged/retry.mjs:14` enables the per-case retry only for the `daily` and `release` profiles, so this run retried one failed journey:

   ```
   Repeating 1 failed case(s): playwright:test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts::mocked/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec/custom%20URL%20remains%20complete%20after%20refresh%20and%20is%20prefilled%20for%20editing
   ```

2. `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:487-491` names the retry result directory `<batchKey>-retry`, i.e. `mocked-standard-config-global-retry`, and passes it as the retry's `CI_RESULTS_DIR`. `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs:183` uses it for the isolated `.ci/run-e2e.sh` child (the job log shows the retry worktree `.ci-retry/mocked-standard-config-global-retry`).

3. `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs:25-31` (`batchLaunchConfig`) reuses the failed case's batch launch config, including `checks: 'run'` when that batch carries the 9 JiuwenSwarm checks (`test/support/tagged/execution.mjs:177,199` keeps them exclusively on `mocked-standard-config-global`). The retry therefore re-ran the supplemental checks on the retry stack — the job log shows all nine (`history`, `history-names`, `run-shell`, `host-tools`, `approvals`, `skills`, `skill-switch`, `trajectory`, `language`) a second time at `16:22:52Z`-`16:23:25Z`.

4. `.ci/run-e2e.sh:448` writes that evidence to `$CI_RESULTS_DIR/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`, so the retry produced `mocked-standard-config-global-retry/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json` inside `.ci-results`, which `.github/workflows/ci.yml:688-696` uploads wholesale as the `mocked-e2e-results-standard-config` artifact.

5. `.ci/mocked-report.mjs:36-39` (added by the merged PR #1361, commit `92f40dab9`) audits **every** `mocked-*` sub-directory of a shard artifact and fails with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS` for any of them other than the single designated check batch that contains `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`. The retry directory is not one of the plan's batches (`mockedBatches()` derives only `-fresh`/`-global`), so the legitimate retry evidence is classified as out-of-bounds.

In short: the audit behaves as written, but the retry path now produces evidence that no accounting consumes and that the audit necessarily rejects. Both halves predate the failure individually; they were only combined when the audit was widened in #1361.

#### Trigger conditions and impact

- Only `daily` (Nightly) and `release` runs can hit it, because only they retry failed cases (`retry.mjs:14`). `pr` and `merge_group` (`merge`) runs never create a `*-retry` directory, so PR CI and the merge queue are unaffected.
- Within a run, it needs a first-attempt failure in the **`mocked-standard-config-global`** batch, i.e. the lane that carries the nine supplemental checks. A retry of `-fresh`, `-global-2`, `standard-journeys`, `research`, `governed` or `literature` runs with `CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS=off` and leaves no checks file, so it does not trip the audit today.
- Consequence: a green mocked layer (195/195, as here) is reported as `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`, the whole Nightly/Release gate is red, and the release evidence shows a mocked failure that did not happen.
- Secondary cost of the same defect: the retry re-runs nine live JiuwenSwarm checks (about 45 s of extra stack work), and any spurious check failure on that second stack turns into `PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED`, a flakiness source unrelated to the one case being retried.

### Verification performed

- Read the failing job log (`Reconcile mocked results`, `Report the outcome`), the green mocked job log (`Repeating 1 failed case(s)` at `16:20:52Z`, the retry worktree, and the second run of the nine checks), and the code paths cited above at `e63099ab`.
- Reproduced with the real code: built a `daily` plan plus worker artifacts via `createPlan`/`verifyResults` and ran `reconcileMocked()` from `.ci/mocked-report.mjs`.
  - Without the retry directory: `PASS 0 []`.
  - After adding only `mocked-e2e-results-standard-config/mocked-standard-config-global-retry/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`: `FAIL 1 ["standard-config: UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS"]` with `planned 5; executed 5; passed 5` — the same shape as the reported `Planned 195; executed 195; passed 195.`
  - Running the same reproduction against `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` at `92f40dab9^` (before PR #1361) returns `PASS` in both cases, which pins the regression.
- The first-attempt failure that triggered the retry (`test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts:277`, `toBeVisible()` on the prefilled proxy URL) passed on retry and is not part of this issue; it is ordinary product/journey flakiness absorbed by the retry policy.

### Suggested bounded fix

Make the isolated retry re-run only what it retries — the failed case — and never the exactly-once supplemental checks:

- In `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`, have `isolatedRetryConfig()` (or `batchLaunchConfig(..., { retry: true })`) emit `checks: 'off'` regardless of `batch.checks`, so `batchLaunchEnvironment()` sets `CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS=off` for a retry. The retry verdict already comes from its own Playwright report (`SCIENCE_TAG_PW_REPORT`), and the first attempt's checks evidence stays authoritative.
- Keep `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` strict. Do **not** simply whitelist `*-retry` there: that would silence a real duplicate-checks run instead of preventing it. If a defensive allowance is still wanted, accept a retry directory only when it holds no `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`, and keep every other `mocked-*` directory failing with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`.

Suggested regression tests (both fail before the fix, pass after):

- `test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs`: `batchLaunchEnvironment(isolatedRetryConfig({ ..., batch: { group: 'mocked', fixture: 'standard', checks: swarmChecks } }).launchConfig).CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS === 'off'`. Today only batches with `checks: []` are covered; a checks-carrying batch returns `'run'`.
- `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs` or `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: a shard artifact containing a `mocked-standard-config-global-retry` directory without checks evidence still reconciles `PASS`, while a `jiuwenswarm-checks.json` in any other `mocked-*` directory still yields `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS` (so the audit's intent is preserved).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-26.04` runner, Actions runner `2.338.2`, workflow `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (Nightly #113) calling `ci.yml` via `workflow_call`.
- Inputs: `profile=daily`, `backend=jiuwenswarm` (repository variable default), `max-parallel=2`; matrix shard `standard-config` with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`.
- The failing step ran `node .ci/mocked-report.mjs .ci-mocked-plan/plan.json .ci-mocked-results .ci-results` at `19:40:01Z`.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main @ e63099ab3b0b2bb30e9ecea432ee6be69efcc8a1` (run head and tested SHA).
- Regression introduced by `92f40dab9b1a1cf65a6716ced5459afc321f38a0` ("ci: run standard mocked E2E shards across 2 isolated local stacks", merged as PR #1361), which added the `mocked-*` directory audit in `.ci/mocked-report.mjs`; the retry directory and its `checks: 'run'` launch config existed before it (`bdc81300b`, "fix: isolate tagged case retries").
- Nightly #111 (`dfdcc9eb`, 2026-11-26) is the last dispatch run in the same series that stayed green, and it had no retried mocked case.

1509.body:
## User outcome

A reader of a literature report can tell what was searched, what could not be searched, how evidence was selected, and why the report uses its output language.

This consolidates the unfinished scope of #416 and #419. Their original reports, artifacts and screenshots remain the historical evidence. This is an administrative consolidation, not a claim that either feature has been delivered.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Saved literature reports include a concise Methods/Search section naming sources actually used, fallback sources, search date, queries and applicable date/language filters.
- [ ] Record retrieved/screened/included counts when measured. Otherwise state "not computed"; never invent counts or imply a systematic review for a brief scan.
- [ ] Disclose source failures and resulting coverage limitations. A provider failure must not silently narrow the evidence while the report claims broader coverage.
- [ ] State the preprint, grey-literature and non-English inclusion policy, or explicitly mark these categories out of scope. Do not require every brief scan to search every category.
- [ ] Define and document report-language behavior for explicit language requests, English/Chinese UI locales and no explicit output-language request. An English report answering an English prompt is not itself a defect. Provide a locale-aware summary if that is the selected policy.
- [ ] Validate saved artifacts as well as the visible report using the original brief CRISPR/SCD scan and deterministic provider fixtures covering fallback, provider failure and unavailable counts. Verify explicit language requests and both UI locales; report real-provider verification separately from mocked coverage.

## Boundaries

Claim excerpts, citation fidelity, unverifiable evidence states and Quick/Deep review coverage remain in #669. A mandatory standard-of-care comparison table is not part of this issue; that optional template proposal is recorded in #417. Keep disclosure proportional to a brief scan and avoid turning it into a mandatory systematic review.
1509.title: [Feature] Disclose literature search methods, coverage and report-language policy

## Purpose

Track the remaining first-use validation and onboarding materials from #22 as a finite delivery task. Closing the original umbrella is administrative, not proof that its entire acceptance passed.

## Existing work and ownership

- One-click sample data, automatic Project/Session creation and the prefilled analysis prompt remain in #566.
- Model registration entry points and save semantics remain in #692.
- Use those issues for implementation rather than duplicating their scope here. File concrete setup/recovery defects found during validation separately and link them below.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Define one supported released-version journey: obtain/open the app, connect a model, upload the supplied licensed CSV, produce a useful chart, request a refinement, save/export and reopen the work. Name the release, supported computer types and sample-data licence.
- [ ] Verify that journey in English and Chinese, including discoverable start actions, language switching, minimum model setup with a connection test, early compatibility feedback, and errors that preserve user input and provide a recovery action. Record actual outcomes and link remaining blockers; do not claim untested platforms pass.
- [ ] Publish and link a 5-7 minute first-result walkthrough from the project entry page, with sample file, prompt, transcript, English/Chinese captions, prerequisites and accelerated waits labelled.
- [ ] Publish and link the 6-8 minute comparison requested in #22: the same IMO 2026 Day 2 Problem 5 task with the same model and comparable budgets, direct conversation versus ScienceDiscovery. Verify the problem/reference and proofs before publishing; report the observed outcome, actual time and cost, including ties or failures. Preserve the original reference links and full solution-family requirement from #22.
- [ ] Observe ten unfamiliar users attempting the sample journey, including users who have not watched the videos. Report unaided completion and friction points; eight of ten is the proposed target, not an existing result. Fix or separately track blocking friction and record next-week return observations when available.
- [ ] Verify the entry page exposes a working help/feedback route and the current GitHub contribution route. Provide a short first-contribution guide, bounded starter tasks with named reviewers, and checks runnable without paid models or special hardware; explain how remaining validation is supported.
- [ ] Publish a final result with release/SHA, journey evidence, materials links, user observations and the disposition of every linked blocker. Assign owners when delivery is scheduled; no owner or deadline is implied by this cleanup.

## Historical context

#22 preserves the original trial feedback and broader product goals. Its old GitCode contribution-routing statement must not be copied as current guidance. Existing delivered UI behavior is a baseline to verify, not a request to reimplement it. New paid runs, user recruitment and publication are future delivery work, not actions performed by this triage.

1511.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1511.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Nightly run [46080401663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663) (`main` @ `a70ef94`, `workflow_dispatch`, `profile: daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`) fails on exactly one real case: shard `research-8`, PUCT-COMPRESS. The in-job isolated retry repeats it on a second, fresh stack and fails the same way.

**Evidence** (job [140778085432](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663/job/140778085432)):

```text
attempt 1        01:18:42  ✘ test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:43  (19.3m)
  Error: Search result code must be persisted as an artifact
  expect(received).toBeTruthy()  Received: undefined
  - Timeout 30000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
  > 172 | }, { timeout: 30_000, message: "Search result code must be persisted as an artifact" }).toBeTruthy();
        at test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:172:93

isolated retry   01:39:08  ✘ test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:43  (18.6m)
  same error, same line, run in .ci-retry/real-standard-retry (fresh worktree at a70ef94)
```

Shard accounting (`real-e2e/tagged/summary.json`, printed in the same job):

```text
| e2e-real | `a37b5e87e214` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
{"status":"FAIL",...,"passed":0,"failed":1,"provider_fault":0}
- e2e-real: PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED: 1
```

Both problem codes are the retry's own exit classification, not a provider outage: `PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED` is `retryFailed(code)` from `test/support/tagged/retry.mjs` ("the retry process itself failed before producing a usable final result", here exit 1 after the case failed again), `PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED` is the first batch exiting non-zero without a recovered case (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:554`), and `provider_fault: 0` means the provider-fault detector (`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`) found no gateway status or transport vocabulary in either failure text. "Account for real cases" ([job 140838600386](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663/job/140838600386)) reports the same single failure: `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21; provider faults 0.`

**The search finished; only the delivery assertion failed.** Before line 172 the case already asserts, and passes:

- line 146: `expect(["succeeded", "budget_exhausted"]).toContain(search.status)` — the search reached a terminal state;
- line 151: the `search_finished` event agrees with the persisted run;
- line 157: `expect(expectedHash).toBeTruthy()` — the finished event names a result node (its `bestNodeIndex`) and a code hash.

So this is neither "the evolve search did not run" nor "the delivered code was queried wrongly".

**Why no artifact exists when the search finished.** Publication is a deliberately narrow path:

- `services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.ts:888-905` (`finish`): the winner is handed to the publisher only when `status === "succeeded" && bestNodeIndex !== undefined`. A `budget_exhausted` run records its state and publishes nothing.
- `services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.ts:910-925` (`publishWinner`): returns without publishing when no `expanded` event carries `bestNodeIndex`. That is the node-0 / seed case: no candidate beat the starting point, so there is no result to save. Intended, and pinned by the UT "nothing is published when the seed won" (`orchestrator.test.ts:928`).
- `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:346-348` (`publishResult`): returns silently when the winner source cannot be read.

Therefore one of exactly two outcomes produced this failure, and the case's own earlier assertions already confine it to them:

1. `search.status === "budget_exhausted"` — the control plane tripped the token/cost gate (`tripBudget`), the sidecar stopped, no artifact is published; or
2. `search.status === "succeeded"` with `bestNodeIndex === 0` — the seed stayed best, no artifact is published.

The spec accepts both statuses at line 146 and then still requires an artifact at line 172, so for either outcome the assertion can never pass. Its comment at line 163, "If the seed stayed best, its original artifact is also valid delivery", is not achievable either: the seed version is created only inside `publishResult` (`platform.ts:354`), which is never called on that path. The documented product behavior agrees with the code, not with the spec: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md:88` says only that *a search with an improvement* saves the starting point and the best code as two versions of the same result artifact.

**Why a race or a wrong query path is ruled out.** `finish` awaits `publishWinner` before the terminal record is published to subscribers, and the case looks for the artifact only after it has seen the terminal status (its own loop polls every 10 s) and re-read the `search_finished` event, then polls for another 30 s. If publication had happened, it would already be committed when the poll starts. The routes the case uses (`GET /api/sessions/:id/artifacts`, `.../artifacts/:id/versions`, `.../artifact-versions/:id/content`) are the ones the product exposes, and the same code passed this case the previous night.

**Impact.**

- Nightly/L5 goes red for a search that legitimately completed with nothing to deliver — the case's own criterion ("search finished normally") is met while its delivery criterion is unreachable.
- The failure costs two ~19 minute paid runs (attempt + retry) and cannot be told apart from a real delivery bug by reading the log.
- Every skip path above is silent: no `apiLog` line records "finished, but nothing published", so the only symptom is a 30 s predicate timeout with `Received: undefined`.
- A user who lets an evolve search run out of budget sees a finished search with no result artifact and no explanation of why.

**Suggested fix.**

1. *Use case (recommended, smallest change).* Make the delivery assertion follow the outcome the search actually had: require the artifact, its version hash and its content only when `search.status === "succeeded" && bestIndex > 0`; otherwise assert the terminal state and keep recording the scorecard, with a comment naming the product rule (nothing to deliver when the seed won or the search stopped on budget). The hash-selection and content assertions stay unchanged for an improving search.
2. *Product (a maintainer decision, not a test fix).* Publish the best-scoring candidate also on `budget_exhausted`, because the sidecar already gave that candidate its held-out score — only if the intended meaning is "a budget stop still delivers its best result". This changes the documented behavior above and the pinned UT.

Either way, add one `apiLog.info` when publication is skipped (`bestNodeIndex === 0`, `status === "budget_exhausted"`, or a candidate-read miss) so the next occurrence names its reason instead of a bare predicate timeout.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-26.04` runner, workflow **Nightly** (`workflow_dispatch`), `profile: daily`, `CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash` over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, bubblewrap sandbox, `E2E_PUCT_LLM_EVALUATION=1`; `E2E_EVOLVE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` unset, so the case's 7 200 000 ms budget applies (not the cause: both attempts ended after ~19 min).
- Per-shard stack: adapter on 4410 in front of the Node API on 4510, runner on 4411, memory-graph, evolve sidecar. The retry ran in `.ci-retry/real-standard-retry` with its own data dir and its own stack.

1515.author: yuanzhou75
1515.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The workbench search box finds Projects, Sessions and artifacts by **name and title only**. Typing a phrase that exists only inside a conversation returns the empty state, so a user who remembers what was said but not the Session title cannot find that Session.

Verified on `main` `e374837d`:

| Piece | State |
| --- | --- |
| Route | `GET /api/search?q=&limit=&offset=` — `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2052-2056` → `searchWorkbench` (`services/api/src/workbench/index.ts:28-102`) |
| What is matched | Project **name** (`:50`); Session **title**, plus its project name and Session id (`:62`); artifact **name/title**, plus its Session title and project name (`:78`) |
| What is not matched | **message bodies.** `searchWorkbench` never calls `store.readMessages`, and `SessionStore` has no text index: a Session's transcript is one JSON file read whole (`services/api/src/store.ts:7319-7327`) |
| Desktop surface | the magnifier in the Session column's title row, `apps/desktop/src/views/SearchDialog.tsx`; `apps/desktop/src/api/workbench.ts:18-23` states the limit in a comment ("not message bodies") |
| Web surface | the same route from `apps/web/src/api/web.ts:75-77` |
| Current UI copy | `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:349` "输入以搜索会话、项目和产物。"; `:353` empty state "没有匹配「…」的会话、项目或产物。搜索只匹配名称与标题，不包含消息正文。" (`en.ts` mirrors both) |

**This is not a regression.** #1251 scoped the search to names and titles on purpose, and its design note 4 asks the field to be honest about it: "Message-content search is a real user need, but `searchWorkbench` only reads titles today; adding it means an index and belongs to a follow-up once this UI exists." The follow-up is this issue.

Reproduction (desktop, current `main`):
1. Click the magnifier in the Session column's title row.
2. Type a phrase that appears in a message body but in no Project name, Session title or artifact name.
3. Observed: 「没有匹配「…」的会话、项目或产物。搜索只匹配名称与标题，不包含消息正文。」 — the conversation containing the phrase is not found, however distinctive the phrase is.

## Design Ideas

The cost is the open question: nothing indexes message text, so a content search has to either read transcripts per query or keep an index.

1. **Bounded scan, no index.** On a content search, read `readMessages` for the Sessions in scope and match the needle. Cheap to write, but it is one full `JSON.parse` of a transcript file per Session per keystroke — acceptable only with a strict scope (for example the current Project, or the most recently updated N Sessions) and a documented depth limit.
2. **In-memory text index, built lazily.** First content search builds Session id → lowercased transcript text, refreshed when a Session's message file changes. Bounded by `limit`, reset on restart. More code, and the memory ceiling and refresh trigger have to be stated.
3. **What a hit is** is a product choice, and the two options differ in client work:
   - **Session hit with a snippet** — the existing `kind: "session"` result, with the matching line in `detail`. No new result kind, so the desktop dialog and the web palette render it as they do today; both copy strings above must change, because they promise the opposite.
   - **Message hit** — a new `kind`, able to open the Session at that message. Needs the shared schema, the desktop filter chips and icons, the web palette, and the contract case in `test/contract/routes.json`.

Whichever is chosen, the copy in `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` / `en.ts` has to be rewritten in the same change: the hint and the empty state currently tell the reader that bodies are not searched.

Sequencing note: PR #1256 (open) edits the same desktop text files and the Session column; it is `dirty` against `main`, so the fix should not race it on those files.

## Involved Public APIs

`GET /api/search` is public and consumed by both clients. A Session-with-snippet fix changes no field; a message-hit fix adds a `kind` value to `WorkbenchSearchResult` and a field for the message anchor, so the shared schema and `test/contract/routes.json` move with it. Paging (`limit`/`offset`, `hasMore`, `total`) must keep meaning the same thing when a second matching source is folded in.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `SessionStore` (`services/api/src/store.ts`) — reading transcripts, and any index refresh hook tied to message writes.
- Desktop Session column and its search dialog; web composer palette — both consume the same response.
- No change to Message, artifact or research storage.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Unit (`services/api/src/workbench/index.test.ts`): a Session whose title and artifacts do not contain the needle but whose transcript does is returned when content search is requested and is not returned when it is off; the needle is matched case-insensitively and only in message bodies, not in stored JSON keys; `limit`/`offset` still page a mixed result set without duplicates or gaps.
- Index path, if an index is built: the index reflects a Message appended after the first build, and a deleted or renamed Session drops out.
- Performance: name a measured ceiling for a fixed number of Sessions (for example 200 Sessions, and the same with the largest transcript in the fixture set) and record the observed number in the pull request, rather than asserting "fast".
- Desktop/web: mocked `GET /api/search` fixtures that include a content hit, plus the empty state and error state; the copy assertions cover the new wording.
- Contract: the `test/contract` case for `GET /api/search` keeps its shape, or gains the new kind explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Typing a phrase that exists only in a message body returns the conversation that contains it; typing a phrase that exists nowhere still shows the empty state.
- [ ] A Session that matched by title is not duplicated when its transcript also matches.
- [ ] The search copy no longer claims that message bodies are not searched, in both `zh-CN` and `en`.
- [ ] Paging, sort order and the kind filters behave as they do today.
- [ ] A stated cost bound: the measured latency at the documented Session-count ceiling, recorded in the pull request.
- Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

1520.author: yuanzhou75
1520.body:
## What happens

Exporting a session, then importing the file that was just written, fails — and the failure depends on what the session's records contain. Two different errors, both seen by the reporter on `main` today, both reproduced here against the exported files:

1. **`File not found`** (HTTP `404 {"error":"File not found"}`, shown as-is in the import dialog). The export succeeds and the file is on disk; the import dies.
2. **`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')`** (HTTP `400` with that JavaScript message as `error`). A different package from the same batch.

These are not upstream/downstream of each other: they are two independent assumptions in the import (`restorePackage`) path, triggered by two different record shapes, in two different packages. Both fail *after* the `inspect` step returns `200` with a valid manifest, so the dialog has already shown the package's contents and title when the import breaks.

## Reproduced

Harness: the in-process API server the repository already uses for import/export tests (`createApiServer` from `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, empty temporary data directory, mocked capacity), driven with the same two requests the desktop dialog makes: `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/inspect` with the file bytes, then `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/import?inspectionChecksum=<checksum>` with an empty body.

| file | size | inspect | import |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `脓毒症内型评分聚类分析_20261128_1240.sdresearch` | 3,087,068 | 200 | **404 File not found** |
| `脓毒症内型评分聚类分析_20261128_1244.sdresearch` | 3,087,061 | 200 | **404 File not found** |
| `自来水中余氯快速比色检测三方案_20261128_1245.sdresearch` | 32,921,173 | 200 | **400 Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')** |
| `新冠刺突蛋白表位 官方DeepSeek_20261128_1248.sdresearch` | 511,345 | 200 | 201 |

SHA-256 of the four files, in that order: `2b375654ba62f5ece7e74a1c4f2cf28477d294b52832798975f5b446b9a4e69b`, `ca4e7c0d1475b6859935e9e0974b8d618ddeed7b0efa95a2322fe4848dd43ece`, `d3dcdbe9c607aa8beff8108d135c03f2687e7ff78cff7bc2860881735b9f6cf3`, `f508a26984c38913a9235285578a513d41288811254e3e50b6cd03d3ecb2fec0`. They are the reporter's own packages and stay on his machine; two later exports of the same sessions (`…_20261128_1309`, `…_20261128_1311`) import with `201`, so this is not "imports never work" — it depends on the records below.

## Root cause 1 — `records.versionObjects` names objects the archive does not carry, and the restore asks for them as if it did

Stack of the 404 (logged from the server's `code === "ENOENT"` branch):

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…/research-package-uploads/research-package-inspect-2GvSVv/objects/8a702d69f0de171b62fb3793143ede9c557191265a1a75e8ac6121be7eed3283'
    at Object.openSync (node:fs)
    at readFileSync (node:fs)
    at DirectoryObjects.get (packages/research-package/src/index.ts:674)
    at <anonymous> (services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1160)
    at async persistImportedResearchPackage (services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1513)
    at async Server.<anonymous> (services/api/src/http/index.ts:1895)
```

`research-snapshots.ts:1159-1162` walks `records.versionObjects` and calls `imported.objects.get(ref.digest.slice(7))`, guarding the result with `if (object)`. For the in-memory import (`importResearchPackage`) `objects` is a `Map`, so a missing entry yields `undefined` and the guard works. The HTTP import uses `importResearchPackageStreamed`, whose `DirectoryObjects` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:670-684`) implements `Map` over files on disk — its `get` is `readFileSync(...)`, so a digest that is not in the archive **throws** instead of returning `undefined`. The two import paths therefore disagree on their own interface (`PackageObjectDirectory extends ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array>`).

What is missing, from the package itself:

* `manifest.omissions` already lists **271** `version:…` entries for this package — the exporter knew those objects could not be read.
* `records.json` still carries all **271** refs in `versionObjects` (pool `agent-state`, e.g. `sha256:8a702d69…`), and 271/271 are absent from `objects/` and from the inventory.
* The digest the restore dies on, `8a702d69…`, is a `workspaceSnapshot.digest` referenced 26 times in `records.json`.

So the package is honest (its manifest says the versions are missing) and the import dies on the very first one instead of importing and reporting the 271 omissions it already carries. Every session whose run records reference `agent-state` version objects that are not stored at export time therefore produces an **unimportable** package.

## Root cause 2 — a `references` key inside tool-call records is treated as a composer reference

Stack of the 400:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
    at ResearchPackageIds.id (services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:26)
    at visit (services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:106)
    at <anonymous> (services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:102)
    … (run-event tree: sessions[0].runEvents[0].streams[1].events[51] …)
```

`remapRunEvent` decides by **key name only**: line 104 treats any object reached under a key called `references` as a `ComposerReference`, and line 106 does `ids.id(reference.id)` for anything whose `kind` is not `skill`/`dbrecord`. Connector/tool records keep their own citation list under exactly that name: this package has **8** objects like

```json
{ "refsource": "Water Res. 2015 Nov 1;84():378", "reftype": "Erratum in", "pmid": "", "note": "" }
```

inside `…step.details.records[0].structuredData.references` — no `kind`, no `id`. `ResearchPackageIds.id(undefined)` calls `source.match(...)` and throws, so the import answers `400` with the raw JavaScript message, and the dialog shows it verbatim.

## Suggested fix

* **Import tolerance (the 404):** ask `has()` before `get()` at every `imported.objects.get(...)` in `restorePackage` (`research-snapshots.ts:1066`, `:1153`, `:1160`, `:1243`, `:1281`, `:1327`), or make `DirectoryObjects.get` total (return `undefined` for a path that is not in the package) so the streamed and in-memory paths behave the same; a version object that is not in the package should become an omission (`version:<pool>:<digest>:missing object`), the way an absent workspace object already is.
* **Remap by shape, not by key name (the 400):** only treat an object as a `ComposerReference` when it actually is one (e.g. `typeof reference.id === "string"`), or only remap the composer's own `references` arrays, leaving `structuredData.references` untouched.
* Both should be pinned with a test built from a package that carries (a) a `versionObjects` entry whose object is absent and (b) a run event whose `structuredData.references` holds citation records.

## Environment

* Desktop app built from `main` (exported 2026-11-28 12:40–12:48 CST, `Asia/Shanghai`), Windows 11.
* Export profile `complete` for all four packages.
* Reproduction ran in WSL against this checkout with the repository's own API server, empty data directory, no model backend; the export side is untouched (the files are the app's own output).

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A long `run_shell` submitted in the background keeps running on the host after the user presses 停止. The run ends in ~300 ms and the composer unlocks, so the UI says the work is over, but the shell keeps running; about 100 s after the cancel the files it writes appear as artifact version 1, and the next user message is answered with that finished task's summary instead of the new question.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. New Session, permission 完全访问, zh-CN UI.
2. Send: `用 python 循环 3 次，每次 sleep 30 秒并打印进度，最后写 progress_a.log。`
3. After ~5 s press 停止. The turn settles in 327 ms with 「已取消」 and the composer unlocks.
4. Send: `改成循环 2 次、每次 sleep 10 秒，写 progress_b.log。`
5. After ~8 s try to send `算了，2+2 等于几？` while it runs — the composer is disabled and the text cannot be typed.
6. Send: `再跑一个：循环 2 次、每次 sleep 20 秒，写 progress_c.log。` After 9 s reload the page and press 停止 again (settles in 299 ms, 「已取消」).
7. Send: `打印 ok`.

**Expected.** Stopping a turn cancels the work the turn started: no new artifact appears after the cancel, and the next message is answered on its own.

**Actual.**

- `loop_progress_c.py` and `progress_c.log` become artifacts (version 1) about 100 s after the cancel — `cc01e1a6-50a8-41b5-88f0-7e61e0918878` and `ef1091f0-59c8-47c2-bf36-51491c72ec20`.
- The answer to `打印 ok` is the cancelled task's completion summary instead of an answer to the question: 「…run_shell 后台提交 loop_progress_c.py（因超过 30 秒前台等待上限），再用 execution_status / execution_logs 跟踪至完成，最后 cat 复核磁盘文件内容一致。 产出 loop_progress_c.py — artifact cc01e1a6…, version 1；progress_c.log — artifact ef1091f0…, version 1」, 283.1K tok.
- The workspace afterwards still holds `loop_progress.py`, `progress_b.log`, `loop_progress_c.py`, `progress_c.log`.

**Where it breaks.** The three 停止 presses all ended the *run* (`run.cancelled`, `reason: "Run cancelled"`), and each one settles in 297–329 ms, so the cancel path itself works. What it does not reach is the execution the run already handed to the Runner: a `run_shell` that exceeds the foreground wait is submitted as a managed Shell Execution that lives in the Runner process (`services/runner/src/server.ts:176` — "Use managed Shell Execution for background tasks"). There is no route in `services/api/src` that cancels a running execution (searching for `cancelExecution`, `executions/:id/cancel`, `stopBackground` finds none), so the abort stops the agent loop but leaves the shell to finish. Its completion is then delivered into the Session and committed as artifact version 1, which is the message the next turn answers.

**Why it matters.** 停止 is the only per-turn escape hatch, and it silently means "stop talking about it", not "stop it". The artifacts are real and versioned, so the workspace and the artifact list disagree with what the user believes happened, and the following answer can belong to the abandoned task.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** #1319 / PR #1321 added a bounded retry for a reasoning-only empty terminal turn, and a readable failure message once the retries are spent. Both live in the JiuwenSwarm gateway. A deployment that runs the **native agent loop** — the default, `createAgentRun`'s `defaultAgentFactory()` — still gets neither: the first empty terminal turn ends the turn, and the message the user sees is the raw transport diagnostic from the model client.

**Minimal reproduction.** Probabilistic, like the original report: it needs the provider to return a turn with `finishReason=stop` and no text and no tool call.

1. Open a Session with a workspace file to analyse; permission 完全访问.
2. Send a normal request: `写一份 1500 字的技术报告，必须引用 3 条证据（记忆或网页），产出 report.md。主题就写 flip.csv 这组 A/B 指标的解读。`
3. On turn 2 the provider returns an empty terminal turn and the run fails about 7 s after it started.

**Expected.** The behaviour #1321 describes, on whichever loop serves the run: replay the empty turn a bounded number of times before failing, and say what happened in user language ("the model returned nothing this round; retried N times") instead of printing transport identifiers in the primary message.

**Actual.** The whole turn is discarded on the first empty terminal turn, with this text (the run's `run.failed` event, verbatim and untruncated apart from the middle of the ids):

```
Model returned an empty terminal turn (no text and no tool call) [requestId=model-8fcbdc57-ba25-49b9-bfa8-cc59661326f9 endpoint=https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com model=deepseek-v4.1-flash httpStatus=200 upstreamRequestId=021795837314155c1c101af9eebb417c253ad03e8acb9414ede40 sseRecords=5 sseParseErrors=0 finishReason=stop hasReasoning=true retries=0]
```

- `status=failed`, `errorCode=server-error`, no retry entry point, and no readable sentence — the string is the one built by `EmptyModelTurnError`.
- `api.log` has no `[model-gateway] retrying an empty terminal model turn` line for this run, i.e. the retry loop never ran.
- Re-issuing the same request as a shorter "methods only" turn succeeded, so the session and the provider were fine.

**Where it breaks (read on `main` @ `e374837`).**

- `services/api/src/agent-run/create-agent-run.ts:56-61` — `defaultAgentFactory()` returns the native loop unless `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` selects the Swarm executor. This deployment runs native.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:537-575` — the empty-turn retry (`MAX_EMPTY_TURN_RETRIES = 2`, `EMPTY_TURN_CLASSES` = `reasoning_only` / `empty_completion`) and `:155-162` `EmptyTurnRecoveryExhaustedError`, which is what writes the readable sentence. Neither is on the native path.
- `packages/model/src/client.ts:1774-1779` — the native path throws `EmptyModelTurnError` straight out of the streamer, and `:168-173` gives it the raw message quoted above.
- `services/api/src/run-failure.ts:44` — that message is then classified as `server-error`, so the failure reads like an internal fault.

**Why it matters.** The empty terminal turn is transient provider behaviour, so on the default loop every occurrence still costs the whole turn — and here a turn is minutes and hundreds of thousands of tokens. The user also cannot tell it apart from a broken environment, which is exactly what #1321 set out to fix.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z): API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner on `4411` (bubblewrap), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Model endpoint: `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, thinking on.
- Session `86b859f7-cc8c-4bca-9073-6e4aa1524956`; failed run `4daf006a-9afe-447d-affb-44293de7457f` (started 2026-11-28T03:41:48Z, failed 03:41:55Z).
- The whole run is 24 events, so the failure is cheap to inspect: `data/run-events/86b859f7-…/4daf006a-…/main.jsonl`.

### Additional Information

- The screenshots attached show the failed turn in the transcript.
- Related, and the reason this is filed separately: #1319 (closed) and PR #1321 fixed the Swarm gateway only. This is the same defect on the loop that the default deployment actually uses, not a re-report of a fixed bug.
- A secondary observation, same message: the raw string carries `requestId` / `upstreamRequestId` / `sseRecords`, so a support conversation about it is a transport-debugging conversation, not a product one.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `services/api/src/agent-run/create-agent-run.ts`, `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/run-failure.ts`.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Three semantically invalid bodies for the sandbox network settings are rejected by the store with a precise message, but the HTTP layer answers `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and logs the real reason as `unclassified_request_error`. A valid body answers 200, so the route and the payload shape are fine.

**Minimal reproduction.** Four requests against a running API, no Session needed:

```
PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":[]}
→ 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"open","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"]}
→ 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"],"bogus":1}
→ 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"]}   # control
→ 200 {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"],...}
```

**Expected.** `400` with the store's own sentence, e.g. `Sandbox network mode domain-allowlist requires at least one allowed domain`, and no `unclassified_request_error` in the log.

**Actual.** 500 with the message replaced. The server log keeps the real reason, so the information exists but never reaches the caller:

```
event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Sandbox network mode domain-allowlist requires at least one allowed domain"
method=PUT path=/api/sandbox-network-settings status=500
```

**Where it breaks.**

- `services/api/src/store/sandbox-network.ts:65-70` throws plain `Error`s whose wording contains none of the tokens `isKnownClientInputError` looks for (`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-38`: `is required`, `must`, `contains an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, …):
  - `Sandbox network mode domain-allowlist requires at least one allowed domain`
  - `Sandbox network mode open does not use allowed domains; remove them or use domain-allowlist`
- The catch-all in `services/api/src/http/index.ts:5295-5300` therefore falls through to 500 and replaces the message with `Internal server error`.
- The same wording-driven mapping also affects `services/api/src/subagent-brief.ts:44` (`${field} requires at least one item`).

**Why it matters.** A caller cannot tell a bad request from a server fault, and the one sentence that would explain the rejection is only in the server log. The desktop client pre-validates the empty allowlist, so today this is reachable from API clients and from any future caller — which is why the fix belongs at the route, not in the wording.

**Suggested fix.** Keep the store's message and answer 400 for these validations — e.g. wrap the PUT handler in `ApiStatusError(400, message)` (this repository prefers typed errors over message matching) rather than editing the wording to contain `must`. Adding `must`/`requires` to the classification keywords is the smaller change but keeps the decision dependent on English wording.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z), API on `127.0.0.1:4410`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- The same numbers were reproduced on `a70ef94` earlier the same day, so this is not new to `e374837`.
- Server log lines: `data/logs/api.log`, 2026-11-28T02:45:31Z.

### Additional Information

- No screenshot: the evidence is the four request/response pairs above plus the log line; the desktop client cannot reach the empty-allowlist case because it validates first.
- The unknown-field case (`"bogus":1`) also answers 500, but I did not trace which validator rejects it; the two store messages above are the ones confirmed in the log.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `services/api/src/store/sandbox-network.ts`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts`, `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, `services/api/src/subagent-brief.ts`.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A running Idea Tree research shows its phase as the raw English word `ideate` in an otherwise Chinese interface, next to the Chinese status (「正在暂停」) and the Chinese round/batch line (「第 0 轮」「本轮 0/1」). The engine emits `ideate`; neither client's phase map has a key for it, so the lookup falls through to the raw value.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. Send `/idea-tree <a purely mechanistic question>` (no web fetching needed), confirm the parameter card, send the command.
2. Wait until `create_idea_research` returns and open the research card (`button.idea-run-card`).
3. Read the progress line: `正在暂停 ideate 第 0 轮 0 tokens`.

**Expected.** The phase is rendered in the UI language — e.g. 「构思」 for `ideate` — like the five phases that do have labels.

**Actual.**

- The progress line prints `ideate`.
- `GET /api/sessions/<id>/idea-tree/research` reports `"phase": "ideate"`, `"status": "running"` (and the engine also persists `phase='ideate'` for a freshly created, paused research).
- `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:212` renders `(t.phase as Record<string, string | undefined>)[research.phase] ?? research.phase`, so an unmapped value passes through untranslated.
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:2625-2631` and `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts:2574-2579` map only `preflight_research`, `building_tree`, `executing_leaf`, `aggregating_score`, `propagating_insight`. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` has the same five.
- The engine really emits it: `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:694` (`s['phase'] = 'ideate'`) and `research_service.py:226` (`phase='ideate'`).

**Why it matters.** Besides the visible English word, `phase` is typed as an open `string` in the shared schema (`packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts:312`), so the compiler cannot catch a phase the text maps do not know: every new engine phase silently degrades to English in both clients. The five labels were written against an assumption about the engine's vocabulary that the engine does not share.

**Suggested fix.** Add `ideate` to the three text maps (one line each, `构思` / `Ideate`), and decide whether the schema should narrow `phase` back to a union of the engine's values so the next addition is a type error instead of an English word on screen.

### Additional Information

- No screenshot: the research used for this report was later ended, so the line is no longer on screen. The payload quoted above (`"phase": "ideate"` from the live research) is the evidence, and the same word is what the progress line prints.
- This is a text-map gap, not a translation-service gap: `ideate` never had a key, and the same word is missing from the English map too (English falls back to itself, so the bug is only visible in Chinese).

### Version Information

1529.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Pressing 暂停 (or 结束) on a running Idea Tree research does not interrupt the model call that is in flight. The status becomes `pausing` immediately and stays there until that call returns; only then, within 0–10 ms, does the research move to `paused` / `ended`. A single call takes 2–3 minutes here, so a 90 s observation shows nothing but `pausing`, and the UI never says what it is waiting for or how long it will take.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. Send `/idea-tree 为什么冰的密度比液态水小？不需要抓网页`, confirm the parameter card, send it, and wait for `create_idea_research`.
2. Once `status: running`, press 暂停 and sample the status and the UI line every 5 s.
3. At 90 s press 结束 and keep sampling until it settles.

**Expected.** Either the pause takes effect promptly (the call is aborted), or the UI says it is waiting for the current model call and for how long ("正在等待当前模型调用返回，最多约 N 秒"), and offers a hard stop that does not wait.

**Actual.**

- 18/18 samples across 90 s: `status: pausing`, progress line 「正在暂停 ideate 第 0 轮 0 tokens」. No explanation, no elapsed wait, no second action.
- `api.log`: this research's five model calls took 146.4 / 149.3 / 153.4 / 187.0 / 190.6 s. Every state transition (`stopped`) lands 6–10 ms after the matching `evolve_llm_call_finished` returns 200 — i.e. the state machine advances on the call's return, not on the request.
- 结束 pressed during `pausing` is queued, not lost: the research finally reads `status: ended`, `reason: "Ended by user"`, `updatedAt 2026-11-28T05:42:35Z`, about 3 minutes after the click. An intermediate read of `paused` means "the pause finished, the end is still queued".
- Asymmetry: `paused → running` through 继续 completes in about 5 s. Entering `pausing` is the slow and opaque direction.

**Where it breaks.**

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py:250-254` — a pause request persists `pendingStop` and sets `s['status'] = 'pausing'`; the SSE stream keeps running, so the UI has nothing but that status to show.
- `research.py` — the engine only observes a stop at `check_stop()` between steps (`Interrupted` is raised there and handled at `:795-796` / `:818-820`). The retry backoff is deliberately sliced so a pause lands promptly (`RETRY_POLL_SECONDS = 0.25`), but the call itself is a single blocking request with no equivalent: nothing can abort it, so the wait is as long as the provider takes.
- The transition to `paused`/`ended` is written after the call returns, which is why the log shows 6–10 ms between `evolve_llm_call_finished` and the activity's `stopped`.

**Why it matters.** The user cannot tell whether the click worked: `pausing` looks identical to stuck, and it can last minutes. It also makes 结束 feel unreliable — two runs of this looked like "the end was swallowed" until the log showed the request had simply been queued behind a 3-minute call. A pause that cannot interrupt anything is a status word, not a control.

**Suggested fix (one of).**

- Abort the in-flight call: pass a cancellation token into the transport (or close the connection) and treat the abort as `Interrupted`, the same way a graceful shutdown already cancels a task.
- Keep the wait but make it honest: in the `pausing` state, show what is being waited on and for how long ("等待当前模型调用返回（已 42 s，最长约 3 分钟）"), and make 结束 apply as soon as the pause settles without a second queue step.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z): API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, evolve sidecar on `17676` (`healthy`, `bwrap`), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`; model Ark `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; permission mode 完全访问.
- Session `b681e51a-8ca2-456c-9df4-02162ac5444e`, research `research-98625896-9d96-4fd2-9c0a-6c1e60bc2ff8`. An earlier research on the same stack (`research-d2b76589-da10-47b0-a113-df7bdbb14394`) also sat in `pausing` for 40 s+ before it settled.

### Additional Information

- This is not the status-persistence family already fixed in #1455 / #1464: the final state here is correct (`ended`, "Ended by user"). The problem is the wait itself and the silence during it.
- Log evidence: `data/logs/api.log` — `evolve_llm_call_finished` (written by `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts:203`) immediately followed by the research activity's `stopped` event, five times, at the call durations above.
- No screenshot of the `pausing` line: the research was ended at the end of the observation, so that state is no longer on screen. The 18/18 sample table and the five call durations in `api.log` are the evidence.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, `research_service.py`, `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts`.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The Runner gives up on managed scientific-environment setup after a single transient network error. Both download steps are tried exactly once:

1. **micromamba provisioner download.** `installManagedMicromamba()` (`services/runner/src/environment-store.ts`) makes one `fetch` to the GitHub release asset. A connect timeout (undici's 10 s default) fails setup with `micromamba setup failed`.
2. **Python base creation.** `bootstrapStarter()` runs one `micromamba create` for the starter packages (python 3.12, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, pysocks) through `executeEnvironmentCommand()` with a 180 s limit. A failure ends setup with `Conda environment setup failed`.

Once setup is `failed`, it stays failed until someone calls setup again. In CI, J3 (`test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts`) and J5 (`test/journey-real-request.spec.ts`) then report `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready`, and the run fails. A user on a flaky or congested network sees the same terminal failure for what is only a momentary blip. The micromamba binary is 18 MB, so retrying it is cheap.

**Observed on 2026-11-28 (merge queue, self-hosted runners).** Between 02:59 and 06:16 UTC, J3 failed 14 times in `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)`:

- 10 × `micromamba setup failed`. From the Playwright trace of `GET /api/environment-setup`, e.g. run [46099537626](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46099537626):

  ```
  Could not download the micromamba provisioner from [network URL omitted] UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT: fetch failed:
  Connect Timeout Error (attempted addresses: 185.199.108.133:443, 185.199.110.133:443, 185.199.109.133:443,
  185.199.111.133:443, timeout: 10000ms) (ManagedProvisionerError / TypeError / UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT)
  ```

  The same error appears in [46100083227](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46100083227) and [46100082508](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46100082508). Each time setup started and failed within about 12 seconds.
- 4 × `Conda environment setup failed`, e.g. run [46099599068](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46099599068). There micromamba was ready, then `micromamba create … --channel conda-forge python=3.12 …` failed. The recorded error holds only the command line, without micromamba's output; #1239 / #1240 cover that diagnostic gap.

The release host was reachable outside those moments: from the same machines, TCP connect took about 1 ms, and 20/20 test connections and 6/6 test downloads succeeded. The failures coincide with peak load. At each failure, 4 of 4 heavy runners on the host were busy, mostly with mocked E2E jobs running two local stacks each.

**Why so much concurrent downloading.** Every mocked E2E stack provisions the managed Python base at start-up. `batchLaunchConfig()` in `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs` sets `scientificEnvs: '1'` for every batch, but only J3 needs a ready base. Each stack therefore downloads micromamba (18 MB) plus roughly 330 MB of conda packages. Several stacks sharing one network egress then hit connect timeouts, and with no retry each timeout is fatal.

**GitHub-hosted runners have not hit this.** Over the previous week (971 `pull_request` and `merge_group` CI runs), none of the 37 failed mocked E2E jobs on GitHub-hosted runners was this failure. All 14 occurrences were on self-hosted runners, where many jobs share a host's egress. The missing retry is a product defect regardless: any user whose connection drops for a few seconds during first-run setup ends up in a failed state.

**Expected.** A transient network failure during managed setup is retried with backoff and recovers without manual action. A permanent failure (SHA-256 mismatch, HTTP 404, unwritable data directory, unsolvable specs) still fails promptly and reports its reason.

**Proposed change.**

- Retry the provisioner download in `installManagedMicromamba()` on network-class failures (connect/read timeouts, connection reset, HTTP 5xx and 429), e.g. 4 attempts with jittered exponential backoff within the existing 120 s budget or a slightly larger one. Do not retry a verify failure (SHA-256 mismatch) or a write failure.
- Retry `micromamba create` / `install` in the starter bootstrap when the failure is network-class, using a fresh attempt directory. micromamba's own `remote_max_retries` / `remote_backoff_factor` / `remote_connect_timeout_secs` could also be set explicitly for these calls. Keep the 180 s command limit per attempt, or make it configurable.
- In the mocked E2E plan, enable `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1` only for the batch that runs J3, so the other stacks stop provisioning a base they never use. This cuts managed-setup downloads in every mocked E2E run on both runner types.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- [ ] A unit test with a fake fetcher that fails with `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` N−1 times and then succeeds reaches `micromamba: ready`. The same test without the change fails.
- [ ] A SHA-256 mismatch and an HTTP 404 are still reported after one attempt, with the existing guidance.
- [ ] The starter bootstrap retries a network-class `micromamba create` failure and still fails fast on an unsolvable spec. Covered by unit tests with a fake provisioner.
- [ ] Only the batch containing `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` runs with `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`. J3 still asserts a ready base and stays BLOCKED when setup really fails.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`, `pnpm ci:ut`, and the mocked E2E shards (`pnpm ci:e2e -- --shard standard-config` at least).

Once this lands, the self-hosted runner image no longer needs its workaround (a pre-placed pinned micromamba via `SCIENCE_AGENT_PROVISIONER_PATH`), and the runners can go back to the Runner's normal managed-download path.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Self-hosted merge-queue runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`): Docker containers on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (kernel 6.8.0-136, x86_64), Docker 29.1.3, Node.js 22.19.0, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7. Several runners share one host's internet egress.
- Managed micromamba pinned at 2.8.1-0 (`services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json`), downloaded from `github.com/mamba-org/micromamba-releases` (CDN `185.199.108–111.133`); starter channel `conda-forge`.
- Mocked E2E entry: `pnpm ci:e2e -- --profile merge --shard standard-config` with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`, JiuwenSwarm backend.

### Additional Information

- Related: #1239 (managed Python base setup failed, J5 BLOCKED; diagnostic gap) and #1240 (include the setup error transcript in the BLOCKED reason). That work makes the cause visible; this issue is about recovering from the transient cause.
- As a stop-gap, the self-hosted runner image currently pre-places the pinned micromamba (`SCIENCE_AGENT_PROVISIONER_PATH`) and shares a persistent `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` across jobs. Since that change, all 16 `standard-config` jobs (each running J3) completed between 06:17 and 07:19 UTC have passed. We would rather keep runner images generic, which is why the fix belongs in the repository.
- Note for anyone using a cache: `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` is not a plain package cache. When set, the Runner switches to `--offline` / `offline-cache` mode, so it cannot be used to cache downloads for an online setup.

### Version Information

`main` at `e89ba7bb3` (2026-11-28). The failing merge-queue candidates were based on `main` around `e374837d3`.
