1532.author: yuanzhou75
1532.body:
## What happens

An import decides twice whether a missing immutable payload is acceptable, and the two decisions cancel each other out.

`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1003` lists the omission texts that mean the copy is not whole:

```ts
const isFatalRestoreOmission = (item: string) => /^(workspace:.*:missing object|artifact:.*:(missing object|no target session)|cas:.*:unavailable|version:.*:unavailable|…)/.test(item);
```

`cas:…:unavailable…` and `version:…:unavailable…` are therefore fatal **only if this import produced them itself**. The filter that consumes the predicate drops anything the package already declared:

```ts
// services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1448-1451
const restoreFailures = omissions.filter((item) => !imported.receipt.omissions.includes(item)
  && !item.startsWith("This package contains no scientific memory snapshot")
  && isFatalRestoreOmission(item));
if (options.sourceSessionId && restoreFailures.length) throw new Error(`…`);
```

`imported.receipt.omissions` is the package's own `manifest.omissions` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:567` and `:808`, copied into `omissions` at `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1109`). A package that honestly declares a lost payload — which is exactly what the exporter writes at `research-snapshots.ts:908` (`version:${key}:unavailable source object`) and `:468`/`:874` (`cas:${hash}:unavailable source object`) — has those strings in the receipt, so they are filtered out and never reach `restoreFailures`.

The same line then decides whether the copy may be continued:

```ts
// services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1475
const continuationAvailable = restoreFailures.length === 0;
```

## What is expected

Two acceptable behaviours, both of which the current code silently skips:

- **refuse the continuation** — a copy that is missing immutable evidence (a version object, a CAS object) is not a base for further research, so `continuationAvailable` should be `false` and starting a continuation should be refused with the omissions named; or
- **downgrade explicitly** — allow it, but say in the receipt and in the UI that the copy is incomplete and what is missing, instead of reporting a clean, continuable import.

What must not happen is what happens now: the package declares the loss, the receipt repeats it, and the copy is still offered as a complete base for 继续研究.

## How to reach it

Any package whose `manifest.omissions` carries `cas:…:unavailable source object` or `version:…:unavailable source object`, imported into a new session (the 继续研究 entry point passes `options.sourceSessionId`, which is the branch that throws on `restoreFailures`).

That is the ordinary shape of a package exported after its payload disappeared: `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts:132-177` builds exactly such a package (blob removed at `:166`, omission asserted at `:167-169`) — only it never imports it, so this path has no test.

The package in #1520 is the same shape at scale: 271 `versionObjects` references, none of their objects in the archive, all 271 named in `manifest.omissions`.

## Why this is not #1520

#1520 and #1521 are about the missing object becoming a `404 File not found` or a raw `TypeError`. With the `get` fix, the missing version object is reported as `version:<pool>:<digest>:missing object` (or already declared) instead of throwing. This report is about the **decision made after** that: the omission is now correctly known, and it is still not allowed to count as fatal. The two can land independently.

## Impact

- A research copy that silently lacks immutable evidence is presented as complete and continuable; the user carries research forward on a base whose versions cannot be restored.
- The receipt already names the omissions, so the information exists and is contradicted two lines later by `continuationAvailable: true`.
- The fatal-omission rule (`:1003`) is effectively dead for the only class of accidental loss the exporter can report — it can never fire, because the exporter always declares what it dropped.

## Environment

- `main` `e89ba7bb3a5555a945b6edb704c7c1e6f2397932`; repository lines above are that commit's.
- Found while auditing the import path for #1520; no runtime reproduction was run (the analysis tree has no installed dependencies), the chain is read from the source above.
1532.title: [Bug]: A copy missing immutable evidence still offers 继续研究, because an omission the package declared can never be fatal

1533.author: yuanzhou75
1533.body:
## What happens

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-39` decides whether an exception is the caller's mistake by matching words in its message:

```ts
return [
  /\bis required\b/i,
  /\bmust\b/i,
  /\bcontains? an unknown value\b/i,
  /\bcannot\b/i,
  /\bdoes not match\b/i,
  /\binvalid\b/i,
  /\bis too long\.?\s*$/i,
  /\bunsafe\b.*\b(?:archive|package|path)\b/i,
  /\bplain basename\b/i,
].some((pattern) => pattern.test(error.message));
```

Anything that matches is answered as a **400 whose body is the raw `error.message`** (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:5216` takes `error.message`, `:5295` sends it with 400). An internal fault therefore becomes a user-visible client error, carrying JavaScript text that was never written for a reader.

Observed instance, from #1520: an import walked a tool record whose `references` array holds literature records rather than composer references; `ResearchPackageIds.id` opened with `source.match(...)` (`services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:26`), so the message was

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
```

`/\bcannot\b/i` matched it, and the client received **`400` with that exact string**. The throw site itself is fixed separately (#1521), but the rule that turned it into a 400 is untouched: the next internal `TypeError` whose text contains *cannot*, *must* or *invalid* will be reported the same way.

## What is expected

- An exception raised by the server's own logic is a **500** with the generic body (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:5296-5304`) and an `unclassified_request_error` line, whatever its message says.
- A **400** comes from something that knows the input was wrong — `ApiStatusError`, `SessionStoreHttpError`, or an explicit code — not from matching prose.
- JavaScript text is never echoed to the client. If a 400 does quote a message, it must be a message that was written to be read.

## How to reach it

Any code path where an in-process fault reaches the request handler. The word list covers the most common accidental shapes:

- `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '…')` — matches `cannot`; this is the #1520 instance.
- `RangeError: Invalid array length`, `TypeError: Invalid value used as weak map key` — match `invalid`.
- `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` — matches `cannot`.
- Any message containing `must` (e.g. a validator that was written for an operator rather than a client).

A minimal, dependency-free check of the rule: `isKnownClientInputError(new TypeError("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')"))` returns `true` — the first pattern that matches is `/cannot/i`, and the function has no other gate.

## Why the word list exists, and why it is a trapdoor

The comment above the function (`error-classification.ts:15-19`) says it is there for legacy validators that still throw plain `Error` objects, and that new handlers should prefer typed errors. That is the right direction, but the fallback is inverted: it guesses *client mistake* from vocabulary, so every future internal fault with the wrong adjective is misreported, while the genuinely unclassified branch (`:5296-5304`) — the one that logs `unclassified_request_error`, which the team uses to find real faults — becomes harder to reach.

## Impact

- Status codes stop being a contract: a caller cannot tell a bad request from a broken server, so clients show an input error for a server fault and retry logic acts on the wrong signal.
- Internal implementation details (function names, property names, class names) reach the UI as text.
- Real server faults are logged at the wrong level or not classified at all, which is exactly what `unclassified_request_error` exists to prevent.
- A malformed import in the same family as #1520 (`400 Cannot read properties of undefined`) is indistinguishable from a correct refusal.

## Environment

- `main` `e89ba7bb3a5555a945b6edb704c7c1e6f2397932`; lines above are that commit's.
- Found while auditing the import path for #1520; the rule itself was read, not exercised on this host (the analysis tree has no installed dependencies).
1533.title: [Bug]: An internal exception whose text says "cannot" is answered 400 with the raw JavaScript message

1535.author: HongyeZhou
1535.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A successful 测试连接 does not produce a short confirmation. The model row turns into one long line that carries the model id, a verdict sentence with a latency, and a permanent 26-character disclaimer:

```
deepseek-v4.1-flash · ✓ 基础检查通过（923 ms） · 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。
```

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. 设置 › 模型 (settings → models).
2. On the configured model's row, press 测试连接 and confirm the paid-token consent when it appears.
3. The test passes in about a second and the row reads as above.

**Expected.** The pass says what the button asked: the connection works. Something like `✓ 连接成功`, optionally with the latency — one short phrase a reader can scan.

**Actual.**

- Three fragments are appended to the row: `· ✓ 基础检查通过（923 ms）` and `· 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。` (quoted verbatim from the rendered row).
- The same verbosity is in the wizard form, where the pass renders two stacked lines — `✓ 基础检查通过（N ms）` and, underneath, `仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。` — and in the web client's own string `基础检查通过 · {latency} ms`.
- The wording also does not answer the question the button asks: 测试连接 → "did it connect?" is answered with "basic check passed", which is a different claim.

**Where it comes from.**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ModelSettings.tsx:139` builds the row text as `TEXT.settings.model.testOk(result.latencyMs)`; `:200-214` renders it inside the row's `<small>` together with the model id, and appends the note in `em.model-row-probe-note` whenever the pass is green.
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1146-1147` (and `en.ts:1112-1113`): `testOk: (latency) => "✓ 基础检查通过（… ms）"`, `testOkNotice: "仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。"`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:668` / `:714` and `zh.ts:1087,1089` render the same two sentences in the add/edit wizard.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:4304`: `"settings.modelTest.success": "基础检查通过 · {latency} ms"`.
- The note is deliberately visible rather than tooltip-only (`ModelSettings.tsx:206-209`, added for #824: "a reader who never hovers still sees what the pass does not prove"), so shortening it must keep that intent rather than hide it in a `title`.

**Why it matters.** The row is a single line, so a pass makes it longer and denser than a failure; the state that should be the quietest ("nothing to do") is the one that wraps or ellipsizes. The sentence a user needs ("connected") is buried in the middle of the line, and the one after it is a caveat that is read on every test.

**Suggested fix (recommended first).**

1. **Short verdict inline, caveat once per list.** Row text becomes `✓ 连接成功（N ms）` (`✓ Connected` in English, latency optional), and the caveat moves out of the row: one muted line under the model list header — "测试连接只验证连通性，不验证完整会话执行、思考或工具调用" — plus keep it in the row's existing `title`. One sentence per screen instead of one per row, and #824's "visible without hovering" still holds because the line is always on screen.
2. **Short verdict only.** `✓ 已连接`, caveat behind the `title` that is already set. Smallest diff, but it drops the visible caveat and reopens #824.
3. **Keep the text, change the layout.** Muted second line inside the row and shorter wording (`✓ 连接成功`); still two lines, but the row line stops being a paragraph.

All three are text/template changes plus one line of layout; option 1 is the one that keeps both the short confirmation and #824's disclosure.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1440x900 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model tested: Ark DeepSeek `deepseek-v4.1-flash` via `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`; the pass took 923 ms.

### Additional Information

- Screenshot attached: 设置 › 模型 immediately after the pass, showing the row as quoted above.
- A failure on the same row reads `✕ <reason>` and is shorter than the pass, which is the inversion this report is about.
- The proxy settings page composes its own result string (`ProxySettings.tsx:71`), so if the wording changes it should change in the same pass or a reader will see two styles of "connected".

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ModelSettings.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts`, `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ProxySettings.tsx`.
